tasks.title: Test smoke and CO detectors
tasks.description: Press the test button on every detector. Replace any that fail.

tasks.title: Clean dryer vent
tasks.description: Pull the dryer out and vacuum the vent hose and wall duct.

tasks.title: Flush the water heater
tasks.description: Drain a few gallons to clear sediment. Hire a pro if the valve is stuck.

tasks.title: Clean refrigerator coils
tasks.description: Unplug and vacuum the condenser coils.

tasks.title: Test GFCI outlets
tasks.description: Press test/reset on kitchen, bath, garage, and exterior GFCIs.

tasks.title: Find and label the main water shutoff.
tasks.description: You want to know this before a pipe bursts, not during.

tasks.title: Label the breaker panel.
Change or rekey the exterior locks.
tasks.description: About $80, or a DIY rekey kit.

tasks.title: Test every smoke and CO detector and note the battery types.
Replace the HVAC filter and record the size.
tasks.description: Put the size in the item’s Size or spec field so the next order is the right one.

tasks.title: Find the water heater and note its age from the serial plate.
Photograph the electrical panel, shutoffs, and appliance nameplates.
tasks.description: Parked in Notes for now.

playbooks.name: Pre-summer AC service
playbooks.why: AC techs book solid by May. A tune-up now costs a service call; a July failure costs emergency rates and a brutal wait.

tasks.title: Service the AC and replace the filter
tasks.description: Book a tune-up before first 100° days. Swap the filter now.

playbooks.name: Monsoon prep
playbooks.why: Monsoon storms arrive fast. Clear drainage and secured loose items prevent the most common summer damage claims.

tasks.title: Check roof and drainage
tasks.description: Clear scuppers and look for cracked mastic before the first storm.

tasks.title: Stage patio furniture and flashlights
tasks.description: Tie down or store furniture. Put flashlights and a charged battery pack by the door.

playbooks.name: Post-monsoon roof and gutter check
playbooks.why: Monsoon debris left on roofs and in gutters bakes in and causes leaks the following summer.

tasks.title: Inspect roof and gutters after monsoon
tasks.description: Look for displaced gravel, clogged downspouts, and stained ceilings.

playbooks.name: Evaporative cooler startup
playbooks.why: Fresh pads and a clean reservoir before first heat — mid-season startup problems always land on the hottest week.

tasks.title: Start up the evaporative cooler
tasks.description: Replace pads, flush the reservoir, and confirm the pump primes.

playbooks.name: Winterize evaporative cooler
playbooks.why: An un-winterized cooler grows scale and mineral damage over winter and shortens pad and pump life.

tasks.title: Winterize the evaporative cooler
tasks.description: Drain the reservoir, disconnect the water line, and cover the unit.

playbooks.name: Irrigation seasonal adjustment
playbooks.why: Summer watering needs change fast in the desert. A seasonal adjustment saves water and keeps plants alive through June.

tasks.title: Adjust irrigation for summer
tasks.description: Increase runtime before heat, then check for broken heads after the first cycle.

tasks.title: Walk drip lines and emitters
tasks.description: Look for clogged emitters, chewed tubing, and dry spots. Flush the filter.

playbooks.name: Dust-season HVAC filter
playbooks.why: Spring dust loads filters in a week. A clean filter before the first 100° day is cheaper than a service call.

tasks.title: Replace HVAC filter before dust season
tasks.description: Swap the filter and set a reminder for 30 days. Recirculate if the air is brown.

playbooks.name: UV caulk and paint inspection
playbooks.why: Desert UV destroys caulk and paint faster than anywhere else. Small touch-ups now prevent stucco and window leaks.

tasks.title: Inspect exterior caulk and paint for UV damage
tasks.description: Walk south and west walls. Recaulk cracked joints around windows.

playbooks.name: Spring AC tune-up
playbooks.why: First 90° week arrives fast. A spring tune-up and fresh filter beat a mid-June service wait.

tasks.title: Schedule AC tune-up and replace the filter
tasks.description: Book service before the first 90°F week; swap the filter now.

playbooks.name: Fall heat inspection
playbooks.why: First freeze is when heat fails. An inspection and filter change in fall is cheaper than an emergency call.

tasks.title: Inspect furnace or heat and replace the filter
tasks.description: Have heat checked before the first freeze; swap the filter.

playbooks.name: Fall gutter clearing
playbooks.why: Leaf-clogged gutters overflow into the foundation and freeze into ice dams.

tasks.title: Clear gutters and downspouts after leaf drop

playbooks.name: Disconnect hoses
playbooks.why: A connected hose can freeze and crack the spigot or the pipe inside the wall.

tasks.title: Disconnect hoses, drain and cover exterior spigots

playbooks.name: Summer humidity check
playbooks.why: Basement humidity above 50% grows mold and rusts ductwork.

tasks.title: Check basement or crawlspace humidity; run dehumidifier under 50%

playbooks.name: Spring sump test
playbooks.why: Spring rains find dead sump pumps. A bucket test is ten minutes.

tasks.title: Test sump pump by pouring a bucket in the pit

playbooks.name: Spring termite walk
playbooks.why: Mud tubes and wood-to-soil contact are early signs. Catching them in spring is cheaper than structural repair.

tasks.title: Walk the foundation for mud tubes; note any wood-to-soil contact

playbooks.name: Storm limb check
playbooks.why: Limbs over the roof and lines come down in summer storms. Trim before peak season.

tasks.title: Check tree limbs over roof and lines; trim or call an arborist

playbooks.name: Furnace service
playbooks.why: Furnace techs book out once the first cold snap hits. A fall service is the cheapest insurance against a mid-winter failure.

tasks.title: Service the furnace
tasks.description: Replace the filter and book a combustion check before first freeze.

playbooks.name: Winterize outdoor water
playbooks.why: One hard freeze with a connected hose can split a pipe inside the wall. Ten minutes now prevents a four-figure repair.

tasks.title: Winterize outdoor faucets
tasks.description: Shut interior valves, open hose bibs, and store hoses.

tasks.title: Blow out or shut down irrigation
tasks.description: Have the system blown out, or close the backflow and drain the lines.

playbooks.name: Fall gutter cleaning
playbooks.why: Leaf-clogged gutters cause ice dams that force water under shingles all winter.

tasks.title: Clean gutters before freeze
tasks.description: Clear leaves so ice dams do not form.

playbooks.name: Chimney inspection
playbooks.why: Creosote buildup is the leading cause of chimney fires. Inspect before the first fire of the season.

tasks.title: Inspect the chimney
tasks.description: Have a sweep check the flue before the first fire.

playbooks.name: Snow equipment prep
playbooks.why: Snow equipment fails the first time you need it. Fuel, oil, and a test run before the first storm.

tasks.title: Prep snow equipment
tasks.description: Fuel the blower, find shovels, and stage ice melt by the door.

playbooks.name: Spring sump pump test
playbooks.why: Spring melt is when sump pumps fail. A test now beats discovering a dead pump with water rising.

tasks.title: Test the sump pump
tasks.description: Pour a bucket of water into the pit and confirm it kicks on.

playbooks.name: Drain exterior spigots
playbooks.why: A hose left on a bib can freeze and crack the valve inside the wall.

tasks.title: Drain and shut off exterior spigots; store hoses

playbooks.name: Attic insulation check
playbooks.why: Thin attic insulation and poor ventilation are the usual ice-dam setup before snow.

tasks.title: Check attic insulation depth and ventilation before snow

playbooks.name: Humidifier pad cleaning
playbooks.why: Dirty humidifier pads grow mold and push it through the ducts all winter.

tasks.title: Clean whole-house or portable humidifier pads; set for winter

playbooks.name: Spring thaw walk
playbooks.why: Thaw reveals grading problems and foundation cracks that freeze hid all winter.

tasks.title: Walk the exterior after thaw: grading, downspout extensions, foundation cracks

playbooks.name: AC condenser startup
playbooks.why: Debris in the condenser and a first-run failure are common after a long off season.

tasks.title: Clear debris from the AC condenser; run it once before the first hot day

playbooks.name: Window weatherstrip check
playbooks.why: Leaky windows and doors waste heat and create ice on the glass.

tasks.title: Check weatherstripping and caulk on windows and doors

playbooks.name: Hurricane prep
playbooks.why: Season runs June through November. Supplies and a plan before the first named storm — stores empty out fast.

tasks.title: Stage hurricane supplies
tasks.description: Water, flashlights, charged batteries, and a go-bag before storm season.

playbooks.name: Dehumidifier and mold checks
playbooks.why: Humidity season feeds mold in weeks. Dehumidifier checks now prevent remediation bills later.

tasks.title: Check humidity and hidden mold
tasks.description: Look under sinks and around the AC closet. Empty dehumidifier tanks.

playbooks.name: Termite inspection
playbooks.why: Spring swarm season is when infestations start. An annual inspection is a fraction of treatment cost.

tasks.title: Schedule a termite inspection
tasks.description: Have the perimeter and attic checked before swarm season.

playbooks.name: AC drain line flush
playbooks.why: A clogged AC drain line backs condensate into the ceiling. A cup of vinegar now beats a drywall repair.

tasks.title: Flush the AC condensate drain
tasks.description: Pour vinegar through the drain to prevent a backup.

playbooks.name: Moss and gutter management
playbooks.why: Wet season feeds roof moss that lifts shingles. Treat before the rains set in.

tasks.title: Clear moss and gutters
tasks.description: Clean gutters and treat moss on the north roof face.

playbooks.name: Post-storm roof inspection
playbooks.why: Winter storms loosen flashing and shingles. A spring check catches damage while it is still small.

tasks.title: Inspect the roof after storm season
tasks.description: Look for lifted shingles and stained sheathing.

playbooks.name: Exterior wood sealing
playbooks.why: Exterior wood only seals well when dry. The summer window is short — miss it and decks absorb a whole wet season.

tasks.title: Seal exterior wood
tasks.description: Recoat decks and trim while the weather is dry.

playbooks.name: Update the home file
playbooks.why: January is when warranties lapse and insurance renews. An hour with the home file finds the gaps before a claim does.

tasks.title: Review appliance warranties and manuals
tasks.description: Check the warranty end dates on the big appliances and file the manuals where you can find them.

tasks.title: Photograph every room for the insurance file
tasks.description: One wide photo per room plus the serial plates on the big appliances, stored somewhere other than this phone.

playbooks.name: Water heater check
playbooks.why: A water heater fails at the age most owners have stopped thinking about it. Check the temperature and the relief valve each winter.

tasks.title: Check the water heater temperature and test the relief valve
tasks.description: Set it to 120°F. Lift the relief lever for a second; water should flow, then stop cleanly.

playbooks.name: Winter indoor air
playbooks.why: Windows stay shut for months. Vents and bath fans carry everything the house breathes.

tasks.title: Vacuum heating vents and bath exhaust fan covers
tasks.description: Pop the covers, vacuum the grilles and the first reach of duct, and wash the bath fan cover.

tasks.title: Wipe down door handles, switches and remotes
tasks.description: Cold-season touch points. One disinfecting wipe on each.

playbooks.name: Laundry deep clean
playbooks.why: Detergent residue and lint build all year. A February clean keeps the washer fresh and the dryer safe.

tasks.title: Clean the washer drum, gasket and detergent drawer
tasks.description: Run a hot cleaning cycle, wipe the door gasket dry, and pull and wash the detergent drawer.

tasks.title: Vacuum behind and under the dryer
tasks.description: Pull the dryer out and vacuum the lint from the floor, the back panel and the exhaust connection.

playbooks.name: Spring refresh
playbooks.why: Winter grime shows in the first bright light. Glass and filters are where it shows most.

tasks.title: Wash windows inside and out
tasks.description: A squeegee and a bucket. Do the inside on a cloudy day so streaks show.

tasks.title: Clean the range hood filter
tasks.description: Soak a metal mesh filter in hot soapy water; replace a charcoal one.

playbooks.name: Irrigation startup
playbooks.why: The first run of the season finds cracked heads and winter leaks before the water bill does.

tasks.title: Run each irrigation zone and fix heads and leaks
tasks.description: Walk each zone while it runs. Straighten tilted heads, clear clogged ones, and mark any wet spot between heads.

playbooks.name: Exterior walk
playbooks.why: Twenty minutes around the outside catches peeling paint, pooled water and cracks while they are small.

tasks.title: Walk the exterior for cracks, peeling paint and pooled water
tasks.description: Siding, foundation, window sills and the ground at each downspout. Photograph anything that changed since last time.

playbooks.name: Fans and filters
playbooks.why: Ceiling fans move dust as much as air. Clean the blades before the fans run all summer.

tasks.title: Clean ceiling fan blades and bath exhaust fans
tasks.description: A pillowcase over each blade catches the dust. Vacuum the bath fan grille.

playbooks.name: Mid-year water check
playbooks.why: Small leaks under sinks and behind toilets run for months unseen. July is the quiet month to look.

tasks.title: Check under sinks and around toilets for leaks
tasks.description: A dry paper towel under each trap and supply line. Any damp spot is worth a closer look.

tasks.title: Test toilet fill valves and flappers for running water
tasks.description: Drop food colouring in the tank. Colour in the bowl after ten minutes means a worn flapper.

playbooks.name: Bins and drains
playbooks.why: Heat turns bins and drains into the smell you cannot find. A wash-out and a flush fix it for the season.

tasks.title: Wash out trash and recycling bins
tasks.description: Hose, dish soap and a stiff brush. Dry in the sun before the lids go back on.

tasks.title: Flush slow drains with hot water and baking soda
tasks.description: Half a cup of baking soda, a cup of vinegar, wait ten minutes, then a kettle of hot water.

playbooks.name: Dishwasher clean
playbooks.why: A clogged filter is why dishes come out gritty. Cleaning it beats a service call.

tasks.title: Clean the dishwasher filter and run a cleaning cycle
tasks.description: Twist out the filter under the lower rack, rinse it clean, then run the hottest empty cycle.

playbooks.name: Disposal refresh
playbooks.why: Ice, salt and citrus peel scour the blades. It is the monthly habit most homes skip.

tasks.title: Clean the garbage disposal with ice and citrus
tasks.description: A tray of ice and a handful of salt, then a few citrus peels with the water running.

playbooks.name: Lights and locks
playbooks.why: Evenings get dark earlier. Working lights and smooth locks are what you notice at the door.

tasks.title: Check exterior lights and replace bulbs
tasks.description: Porch, path and motion lights. Wipe the fixtures while the ladder is out.

tasks.title: Lubricate door locks and hinges
tasks.description: Graphite or a dry lubricant in each lock, a drop of oil on each hinge pin.

playbooks.name: Garage door safety check
playbooks.why: The auto-reverse is the safety feature families rely on and never test.

tasks.title: Test the garage door auto-reverse and lubricate the rails
tasks.description: Lay a board in the door's path; it must reverse on contact. Then a silicone spray on the rollers and hinges.

playbooks.name: Fire safety check
playbooks.why: Heating season is fire season. Extinguishers expire and detectors age out.

tasks.title: Check the fire extinguisher gauge and expiry date
tasks.description: Needle in the green, pin in place, date on the label still good.

tasks.title: Check detector manufacture dates; replace any over ten years old
tasks.description: The date is printed on the back. Sensors fail quietly after a decade.

playbooks.name: Draft check
playbooks.why: Drafts are the cheapest heating loss to fix. Feel for them on the first cold evening.

tasks.title: Check for drafts at windows and doors
tasks.description: Move a lit candle or a damp hand along each frame on a cold evening. Mark the spots that flicker.

playbooks.name: Holiday safety
playbooks.why: December adds cords, lights and heaters to every room. Ten minutes keeps them from adding a claim.

tasks.title: Check extension cords, outlet loads and light strings
tasks.description: No daisy-chained strips, no cords under rugs, and one heater per circuit.

tasks.title: Check space heaters for damaged cords and tip-over shutoff
tasks.description: Tip it gently; it should switch off. Retire any heater with a frayed or warm cord.
